patterns.evidence: Post-lunch hypoglycemia daily 60-72 mg/dL: D1 65, D2 70, D3 62, D4 72, D5 66, D6 64, D7 68, D8 62, D9 60, D10 70. Pattern indicates lunch insulin overdose or high activity.

patterns.name: Dawn Phenomenon
patterns.evidence: Fasting glucose 142-158 mg/dL every day: D1 152, D2 158, D3 148, D4 155, D5 152, D6 145, D7 158, D8 150, D9 142, D10 155. Elevated mornings suggest dawn phenomenon; basal may be insufficient overnight.

analysis.message: 19-year-old T1 male (104 kg) has significant dawn phenomenon and breakfast spikes. Consider increasing basal to 26U or splitting dose. Morning insulin-to-carb ratio needs aggressive adjustment. Afternoon control is decent.

patterns.name: Dawn Phenomenon
patterns.evidence: Fasting glucose 152-170 mg/dL: D1 158, D2 165, D3 152, D4 170, D5 162, D6 155, D7 168, D8 160, D9 153, D10 165. Despite 24U Lantus, morning hyperglycemia persists, indicating need for higher basal or split dose.

patterns.name: Afternoon Stable
patterns.evidence: Evening glucose settles to 130-145 mg/dL after daytime corrections. D1 135, D3 132, D5 138, D6 132, D8 136. Afternoon stability is good.
